title: Draft the solicitation plan brief for a major-gift ask of a donor couple
instructions: Teresa Lindahl, our Director of Major Gifts, wants to ask Martin and Celeste Vandermolen for a gift this fall. Using their CRM record, contact reports and research profile, our funding opportunities and our policies, write the solicitation plan brief our policy calls for — the document Teresa and her leadership partner will both work from.

criteria.title: Ask amount is $80,000
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan's ask is a single figure of $80,000. FAIL if the ask is any other amount — such as $95,000 (the formula figure without the cap, or capped at four times the $25,000 corporate sponsorship), $150,000 (Teresa's guess in the 2026-08-27 note), $100,000 or $50,000 — or is given as a range.

criteria.title: Cap set from the $20,000 donor-advised fund gift
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan caps the ask at four times the household's largest gift to the Foundation, identifying that gift as the $20,000 Adult Literacy gift of 2025-10-14 from the Vandermolen Family Fund (their donor-advised fund), for a cap of $80,000. FAIL if it treats any other gift as the household's largest — such as the $25,000 Vandermolen Marine Supply gala sponsorship (2023), the $25,000 Maritime Heritage Society gift, or the $12,500 gift of 2024 — or applies no cap.

criteria.title: Asks for the Adult Literacy Program, not the building campaign
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan asks the Vandermolens to support the Adult Literacy Program — for example Tutor Corps, learner materials, the Upriver evening site, ESL Conversation Circles or the Adult Literacy Endowment — and offers no Open Doors option. FAIL if the ask, or any alternative offered, is for the Open Doors campaign or the Eastside Branch (including its Adult Literacy Learning Lab), for another program such as Reading Buddies or Teen Makerspace, or for unrestricted support.

criteria.title: Offers no naming opportunity
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan offers or suggests no naming opportunity of any kind. FAIL if it offers or suggests naming anything — the Adult Literacy Learning Lab ($75,000), a room, a fund, a tutoring site or a program — after the Vandermolens or in honor or memory of anyone (such as Celeste's mother), even as an option or a fallback.

criteria.title: Recognition plan honors their anonymity
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan states that the gift will be anonymous — no listing in the annual report, on a donor wall or in any announcement — with private acknowledgment only. FAIL if the plan proposes any public recognition by name (honor-roll or annual-report listing, donor wall, press release, event announcement), uses the CRM's recognition name "Martin & Celeste Vandermolen" for this gift, or does not address recognition.

criteria.title: Directs the ask to Celeste as the decision-maker
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan identifies Celeste Vandermolen as the one who makes the couple's philanthropic decisions and directs the ask to her (Martin may be present and included). FAIL if it treats Martin as the decision-maker, directs the ask to Martin, or plans to win Martin over first — for example because he is the CRM's primary constituent or because of his 2022 interest in a building with the family name.

criteria.title: Reaches them only through personal channels, never the business
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan arranges the meeting and follow-up through Celeste's personal email (celeste.vdm@example.net) or the home phone ((360) 555-0187), and the meeting is somewhere other than the company (for example their home or the library). FAIL if the plan proposes reaching them through Vandermolen Marine Supply in any way — the vandermolenmarine.com email addresses, the store's main line (360) 555-0142, mail to 220 Harbor Way, Martin's assistant — or meeting at the company; or if it does not say which personal channel will be used.

criteria.title: Solicitation team is Teresa Lindahl with Lillian Cho
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan's solicitation team is Teresa Lindahl with board member Lillian Cho as the leadership partner (Celeste asked for her, and she has made her FY27 gift); the Executive Director, Dr. Imogen Hartley, may also attend. FAIL if Lillian Cho is not on the team, or if the team includes anyone other than Teresa Lindahl, Lillian Cho and the Executive Director — such as Peter Lindgren (no FY27 gift yet) or Gregory Hale.

criteria.title: Keeps Gregory Hale out of the solicitation
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan gives board member Gregory Hale no role in cultivating or soliciting the Vandermolens; noting that he is recused, or that his offer is declined, is fine. FAIL if it proposes Hale as solicitor, co-solicitor, leadership partner, door-opener, host or attendee, has him set up or follow up the meeting, or suggests consulting him on how to approach Martin.

criteria.title: Does not disclose the Rasmussens' anonymous gift
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan nowhere discloses the Rasmussen family's anonymous gift — neither the family's or Ingrid Rasmussen's name in connection with a gift, nor its $100,000 amount, nor a description such as "a fellow tutor's family recently gave to the endowment" — in talking points, peer examples, benchmarks or background. A general instruction not to discuss other donors' gifts is fine. FAIL if the plan mentions that gift in any form, or uses it to size or justify the ask.

criteria.title: Times the ask after their mid-October advisor meeting
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the plan sets the ask meeting after the Vandermolens' mid-October meeting with their financial advisor and no later than November, when they make their giving decisions — for example late October or early November 2026. Contacting Celeste sooner to arrange the date is fine. FAIL if the plan makes the ask before their advisor meeting (in September or the first half of October), or after November.

criteria.title: Invents no fact about the donors
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if every fact the plan states about Martin and Celeste Vandermolen — gifts, capacity, assets, family, interests, preferences, quotations — appears in the files. FAIL if the plan states a gift, asset, capacity figure, family member, interest, preference or quotation for them that appears in no file. Arithmetic slips, superseded figures and misapplied rules — a wrong total, a date counted the wrong way, a step a policy forbids — are judged by the task's other criteria and do not fail this one: it fails only on a fact, figure, rule, approval or person with no source in the files, or on something the files attribute to someone else.
